title: Topography-Guided Transepithelial Accelerated Corneal Collagen Cross-Linking for Low Refractive Error Correction in Keratoconus Treatment: A Pilot Study

license.statement: CC BY, version not stated (article <license>: 'distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY)'; no licence URL in the XML)

groups.description: Prospective self-controlled pilot study (Fudan University EENT Hospital): 18 eyes of 18 patients with keratoconus stable for 12 months, low refractive error (SE 0 to -3.00 D), aged at least 18 years (mean 24.88 ± 4.64 years), treated with the investigational topography-guided transepithelial accelerated CXL (0.1% then 0.25% riboflavin without epithelial removal, pulsed UVA 45 mW/cm2 in three concentric zones centred on the maximum posterior elevation, total dose 5.4, 10 or 15 J by corneal curvature, KXL II); one surgeon.

series.notes: mean ± SD; Pentacam (Oculus); 18 eyes treated, one patient withdrew for personal reasons after the operation, so 17 eyes were analysed (baseline n = 17); one patient was lost after the 6-month visit (1-year n presumably 16, not tabulated); 1 week converted as 7/30.4375 = 0.23 months.

exclusions.what: Steep K (R5) and Flat K (R6) rows of Table 1
exclusions.reason: K2 and K1 are not Kmax (protocol inclusion 1)

exclusions.what: Kmax decrease of two eyes stated in the Results text
exclusions.reason: text-only statement, not a tabulated series

notes: Procedure classified cxl_epi_on: the cross-linking is transepithelial (riboflavin applied without epithelial removal), which fits the epithelium-on context; the topography-guided, zonal irradiation pattern is recorded in the group description.
Role 'treated': single-arm pilot of an investigational customized protocol, each eye compared with its own preoperative values.
Age group 'adult': inclusion required age at least 18 years and no patient is reported as 18 or younger; the age range is not stated.
Other tabulated parameters (UDVA, CDVA, SE, TCT, ECD in Table 1) are not used.
